_comment: Every scheduled job on this Mac, with how late it may run before the queue skips it.
maxLateMinutes is the honest question: if this fires now instead of at its cron time,
is the work still worth doing? A nightly sweep landing at 08:30 is noise, so it is
skipped. A Universal Credit check Mica needs is still worth sending at lunchtime, so it
is not. Sweeps get tight limits; anything that touches a person or an obligation gets a
generous one.
mode: 'wrapped' jobs are launchd shell commands run via job-queue.py run, so their PID
proves liveness. 'cooperative' jobs are Claude routines that call acquire and release
from their SKILL.md, where only the lease can free a crashed session.
Crons are standard five-field, LOCAL time, Sunday = 0.
queued:false means the job runs OUTSIDE the queue on purpose. Both such jobs exist to
report on or clean up after the others, so waiting behind a stuck routine would stop them
doing the one thing they are for. They are still listed here so the morning digest watches
needs: what must be true before the job may start. Five of the seven jobs that
failed every day were not broken. They fired the instant the Mac woke, before the
network and Google Drive were up, and reported a hard failure. The queue now waits
up to readyWaitMinutes (default 10) and DEFERS rather than failing if still not
ready. A drive probe READS A BYTE: an unmounted Drive folder still exists and still
lists, and only fails on open with 'Resource deadlock avoided'.
27 Aug 2026: that check runs BEFORE the lock wait, on purpose, so a job waiting for the
network does not hold the queue shut. But the wait is unbounded, and the thing that causes
a long wait here is the Mac sleeping, which is also what kills the network. handback-poll
queued at 08:30 with the network up, waited 43 minutes, took the lock the instant the Mac
woke, and died on DNS. acquire() now RE-PROBES after a wait longer than 60s and DEFERS
instead of failing. The same shape had already hit compound-brain, publish-brain,
masterplan-sync and daily-ops-guard.
8 Aug 2026: the fourteen Claude routines were absorbed into one, `daily-ops`.
Serialising them behind a lock stopped them overwriting each other, then created a
worse failure: a routine suspended by the Mac sleeping keeps HOLDING the lock.
drift-monitor held it 4h54m while asleep, so everything behind it waited and was then
skipped for lateness. A lock cannot fix a machine that sleeps, because the lock sleeps
too. One routine running in sequence has nothing to overlap with and nothing to skip.
The lock now only guards the short shell jobs, and they heartbeat so a sleeping one
frees it in minutes.
them: a job left out of this file entirely is a job nobody notices has stopped.

mac-guard.note: reaps preview servers and test browsers that outlived their session. Must run even while a routine holds the queue, since a stuck routine is exactly when strays pile up

job-digest.note: reports on the queue, so it must never wait behind it

daily-ops.note: THE one Claude routine. Never skipped for lateness (maxLate 1440) — it IS the daily run, and skipping it means nothing happens at all. Unqueued: it runs for an hour or more and must not hold the lock the short shell jobs need.

daily-ops-guard.note: alarms if daily-ops left no phase-1 mark by 08:00 London — the scheduler stamped lastRunAt on 15 Aug 2026 while delivering the run to no session, so only the mark counts. Reports on the routine, so it must never wait behind anything. London gate lives in the code, not this cron (Mac timezone moves with Kevin).

data-invariants.note: Kevin's restructure of 26 Aug 2026: the live Airtable invariants run as a plain script every morning, with no Claude in the loop. Each invariant carries a control that fails the run rather than passing on an empty population. daily-ops reads the result and only applies judgement when it FAILED.

drift-scan.note: Kevin's restructure of 26 Aug 2026: the schema snapshot and dead-reference scan are a diff, not a judgement, so they run as a script. It exits 0 when nothing changed and writes an exceptions file only when it did. The old Claude drift phase was the single largest source of findings (68 open) and its own report called the SOP metric 'red every day and carries no signal'.

drive-auth.note: Kevin's restructure of 26 Aug 2026: scripts/drive-auth-check.py was already a script with its own selftest control. It no longer needs a Claude phase to run it.

task-manager.note: the Task Manager agent's own Go Signal (Kevin, 25 Aug 2026): board pass at the same three slots as inbound-triage. NOT a daily-ops phase by explicit ruling (same pattern as inbound-triage); a headless claude run, so the generous lateness keeps a wake-delayed slot worth running. The queue lock stops it running at the same time as the triage slot job; order within the hour is whichever launchd starts first, and the board pass tolerates either order (dispatch's in-flight tasks are subtracted in code).

handback-poll.note: Kevin's call, 26 Aug 2026, after measuring the approval loop: the agent's own work on a hand-back is a median of FIVE MINUTES, but he waited a median of 3.6 hours over 1-26 Aug because nothing opened the queue between daily-ops (07:00) and the three triage slots. This checks every half hour and wakes a headless claude run ONLY when a hand-back is actually waiting; a quiet tick is one Airtable read and costs no tokens. HAND-BACKS ONLY (carry_out and redo) — new work, routing and escalation stay in the daily slots. Lateness is deliberately tight: a tick more than 20 minutes late is covered by the next one, so a wake-stampede must not run six of these back to back. The job name is NOT a skill folder name, so check-routines.py sees a registered shell job rather than a second Claude routine.

retry-deferred.note: Added 27 Aug 2026. launchd fires a job once; if the machine is not ready the queue DEFERS, and until this existed nothing ever came back, so a defer was a lost day and maxLateMinutes allowed lateness nothing could use. The brain went four days unfed that way (24-27 Aug), Drive being unreadable from a sleeping Mac at 22:45 every night. Hourly at :20, OUTSIDE the queue on purpose - it exists to rescue jobs the queue turned away, so waiting behind a stuck routine would stop it doing the one thing it is for. Only re-fires jobs carrying retryWhenDeferred, and REPORTS any other job that deferred rather than silently passing over it.

mcp-inventory.note: Regenerates js/mcp-tools-data.js, the Tools & Connections list on the AI Agents page, from the real MCP configuration (28 Aug 2026). A pure read of local config files plus one `claude mcp list` health check; no AI, no judgement, nothing written outside the repo. Every source has a floor and the run FAILS rather than writing a shorter list, because a list that quietly shrank would read as a smaller estate instead of a broken read. maxLateMinutes is deliberately huge: this Mac sleeps, and the first manual run SKIPPED at 249 minutes late under the original 240. An inventory of what we are connected to is just as true at 4pm as at 6am, so a late refresh beats no refresh. Runs with --publish: when the list genuinely changes it opens a PR carrying the one file, assembled with git plumbing against a throwaway index so it can never disturb another session's uncommitted work in this shared checkout. It never pushes to main. Before publishing it runs the list's own data-shape tests against the candidate and merges only if they pass; a failure leaves the PR open and exits non-zero so the digest catches it.

signature-watch.note: Polls Adobe for documents that have come back signed and files the signed PDF for Kevin's second approval. Four times a day: a signature can land at any hour and the poll costs nothing when nothing is registered, because it exits before opening a browser. Generous lateness on purpose — a signed document is still worth picking up late. NO day-of-week: people sign at weekends.
